chunks.text:
Clock skew against the exchange exceeds tolerance. Clock skew or lost time synchronisation against the exchange
## Recognise
The component exits or idles with a line that reports clock skew in milliseconds against the exchange and a tolerance it exceeds, and states that it refuses to trade.
chunks.title: Clock skew against the exchange exceeds tolerance
chunks.match: Clock skew or lost time synchronisation against the exchange

chunks.text:
Clock skew against the exchange exceeds tolerance. Clock skew or lost time synchronisation against the exchange
## Why it happens
Time synchronisation on the node drifted or lost its source. Order timestamps outside the exchange's tolerance are rejected, and audit trails with wrong times are a regulatory problem, so the component stops on purpose.
chunks.title: Clock skew against the exchange exceeds tolerance
chunks.match: Clock skew or lost time synchronisation against the exchange

chunks.text:
Clock skew against the exchange exceeds tolerance. Clock skew or lost time synchronisation against the exchange
## Remediate
No automatic action. Restarting the component does not move the clock, and a rollback would restart a healthy binary.
chunks.title: Clock skew against the exchange exceeds tolerance
chunks.match: Clock skew or lost time synchronisation against the exchange

chunks.text:
Clock skew against the exchange exceeds tolerance. Clock skew or lost time synchronisation against the exchange
## Verify
Not applicable until time synchronisation on the node is repaired.
chunks.title: Clock skew against the exchange exceeds tolerance
chunks.match: Clock skew or lost time synchronisation against the exchange

chunks.text:
Clock skew against the exchange exceeds tolerance. Clock skew or lost time synchronisation against the exchange
## Escalate when
Always. Page the infrastructure owner; trading on this node stays halted until the skew is back inside tolerance.
chunks.title: Clock skew against the exchange exceeds tolerance
chunks.match: Clock skew or lost time synchronisation against the exchange

chunks.text:
Crash loop from a configuration error. Configuration error: a setting is missing, empty or invalid
## Recognise
The container starts, prints a fatal line that names a setting, and exits with a small non-zero code. Typical lines: FATAL config: FEED_URL is empty, invalid value for --max-order-size, required key missing. The restart count climbs and the pod state is CrashLoopBackOff. The crashes begin right after a rollout.
chunks.title: Crash loop from a configuration error
chunks.match: Configuration error: a setting is missing, empty or invalid

chunks.text:
Crash loop from a configuration error. Configuration error: a setting is missing, empty or invalid
## Why it happens
The last change removed or emptied an environment variable, a ConfigMap key or a flag. The binary validates its configuration at start and refuses to run, which is the correct behaviour for a trading component: running with a wrong limit is worse than not running.
chunks.title: Crash loop from a configuration error
chunks.match: Configuration error: a setting is missing, empty or invalid

chunks.text:
Crash loop from a configuration error. Configuration error: a setting is missing, empty or invalid
## Remediate
Return the deployment to its previous revision with rollout_undo. The configuration that worked comes back with it. Do not edit the configuration by hand during the incident.
chunks.title: Crash loop from a configuration error
chunks.match: Configuration error: a setting is missing, empty or invalid

chunks.text:
Crash loop from a configuration error. Configuration error: a setting is missing, empty or invalid
## Verify
The pod is Running and Ready, the restart count stops increasing, and the fatal line no longer appears in the log.
chunks.title: Crash loop from a configuration error
chunks.match: Configuration error: a setting is missing, empty or invalid

chunks.text:
Crash loop from a configuration error. Configuration error: a setting is missing, empty or invalid
## Escalate when
There is no previous revision, or the same fatal line appears on the previous revision too. Then the cause is outside the deployment, for example a shared ConfigMap, and a person must decide.
chunks.title: Crash loop from a configuration error
chunks.match: Configuration error: a setting is missing, empty or invalid

chunks.text:
Order gateway lost its exchange session. Exchange session problem: logon rejected, disconnected or connection refused
## Recognise
The order gateway logs a rejected logon, a refused connection to the exchange endpoint, or repeated disconnects. Orders are not acknowledged.
chunks.title: Order gateway lost its exchange session
chunks.match: Exchange session problem: logon rejected, disconnected or connection refused

chunks.text:
Order gateway lost its exchange session. Exchange session problem: logon rejected, disconnected or connection refused
## Why it happens
Credentials expired, the exchange session was already open elsewhere, or the line is down. The gateway may hold working orders whose state is unknown.
chunks.title: Order gateway lost its exchange session
chunks.match: Exchange session problem: logon rejected, disconnected or connection refused

chunks.text:
Order gateway lost its exchange session. Exchange session problem: logon rejected, disconnected or connection refused
## Remediate
No automatic action. Restarting a gateway with working orders can duplicate or orphan them. Order state must be reconciled first.
chunks.title: Order gateway lost its exchange session
chunks.match: Exchange session problem: logon rejected, disconnected or connection refused

chunks.text:
Order gateway lost its exchange session. Exchange session problem: logon rejected, disconnected or connection refused
## Verify
Not applicable until a person has reconciled open orders.
chunks.title: Order gateway lost its exchange session
chunks.match: Exchange session problem: logon rejected, disconnected or connection refused

chunks.text:
Order gateway lost its exchange session. Exchange session problem: logon rejected, disconnected or connection refused
## Escalate when
Always. Page the trading desk and the session owner at the same time.
chunks.title: Order gateway lost its exchange session
chunks.match: Exchange session problem: logon rejected, disconnected or connection refused

chunks.text:
Image cannot be pulled after a rollout. Image cannot be pulled: wrong tag, missing image or registry refused
## Recognise
New pods of the deployment sit in ImagePullBackOff or ErrImagePull. The event text names the image and says it was not found, or that the registry refused the request. Pods of the previous revision are still serving, because the rolling update will not remove them until new pods are Ready.
chunks.title: Image cannot be pulled after a rollout
chunks.match: Image cannot be pulled: wrong tag, missing image or registry refused

chunks.text:
Image cannot be pulled after a rollout. Image cannot be pulled: wrong tag, missing image or registry refused
## Why it happens
A release pipeline pushed a deployment that points at a tag which was never published, was typed wrongly, or lives in a registry the node cannot reach. Nothing is wrong with the running system; the new revision simply cannot start.
chunks.title: Image cannot be pulled after a rollout
chunks.match: Image cannot be pulled: wrong tag, missing image or registry refused

chunks.text:
Image cannot be pulled after a rollout. Image cannot be pulled: wrong tag, missing image or registry refused
## Remediate
Return the deployment to its previous revision with rollout_undo. This removes the broken ReplicaSet and keeps the pods that are already serving. Do not delete pods: the old ones are the only capacity left.
chunks.title: Image cannot be pulled after a rollout
chunks.match: Image cannot be pulled: wrong tag, missing image or registry refused

chunks.text:
Image cannot be pulled after a rollout. Image cannot be pulled: wrong tag, missing image or registry refused
## Verify
Every pod of the deployment is Running and Ready within one minute and no pod is in ImagePullBackOff.
chunks.title: Image cannot be pulled after a rollout
chunks.match: Image cannot be pulled: wrong tag, missing image or registry refused

chunks.text:
Image cannot be pulled after a rollout. Image cannot be pulled: wrong tag, missing image or registry refused
## Escalate when
The deployment has no previous revision, or the previous revision also fails to pull. That means the registry itself is unreachable and a rollback cannot help.
chunks.title: Image cannot be pulled after a rollout
chunks.match: Image cannot be pulled: wrong tag, missing image or registry refused

chunks.text:
Container killed for exceeding its memory limit. Out of memory: container OOMKilled, exit 137, memory limit exceeded
## Recognise
The last termination reason is OOMKilled and the exit code is 137. The log usually ends in the middle of normal work, because the kernel kills the process without warning. There may be no error line at all.
chunks.title: Container killed for exceeding its memory limit
chunks.match: Out of memory: container OOMKilled, exit 137, memory limit exceeded

chunks.text:
Container killed for exceeding its memory limit. Out of memory: container OOMKilled, exit 137, memory limit exceeded
## Why it happens
The working set grew past the container's memory limit: more instruments, a larger position book at market open, or a limit that was set from an idle measurement. A leak looks the same at first, which is why the automatic step is bounded.
chunks.title: Container killed for exceeding its memory limit
chunks.match: Out of memory: container OOMKilled, exit 137, memory limit exceeded

chunks.text:
Container killed for exceeding its memory limit. Out of memory: container OOMKilled, exit 137, memory limit exceeded
## Remediate
Raise the memory limit with set_memory_limit to twice the current value, never above the platform ceiling. One step only. Record the change so that capacity planning sees it.
chunks.title: Container killed for exceeding its memory limit
chunks.match: Out of memory: container OOMKilled, exit 137, memory limit exceeded

chunks.text:
Container killed for exceeding its memory limit. Out of memory: container OOMKilled, exit 137, memory limit exceeded
## Verify
The pod stays Running and Ready for the verification window and the restart count stops increasing.
chunks.title: Container killed for exceeding its memory limit
chunks.match: Out of memory: container OOMKilled, exit 137, memory limit exceeded

chunks.text:
Container killed for exceeding its memory limit. Out of memory: container OOMKilled, exit 137, memory limit exceeded
## Escalate when
The limit is already at the ceiling, or the container is OOMKilled again after one raise. Repeated growth is a leak, and feeding a leak more memory only delays the page.
chunks.title: Container killed for exceeding its memory limit
chunks.match: Out of memory: container OOMKilled, exit 137, memory limit exceeded

chunks.text:
Readiness probe fails after a rollout. Readiness probe fails: pod is Running but never Ready
## Recognise
The container is Running and does not restart, but the pod never becomes Ready. Events repeat Readiness probe failed with the probe's own error, such as a refused connection, a missing file or a wrong path. The Service has no endpoints for the new pods.
chunks.title: Readiness probe fails after a rollout
chunks.match: Readiness probe fails: pod is Running but never Ready

chunks.text:
Readiness probe fails after a rollout. Readiness probe fails: pod is Running but never Ready
## Why it happens
The rollout changed the probe, the port or the path the probe checks, so a healthy process is reported as unready. Less often the process itself hangs during start.
chunks.title: Readiness probe fails after a rollout
chunks.match: Readiness probe fails: pod is Running but never Ready

chunks.text:
Readiness probe fails after a rollout. Readiness probe fails: pod is Running but never Ready
## Remediate
Return the deployment to its previous revision with rollout_undo. Restarting does not help, because the new pods would carry the same probe.
chunks.title: Readiness probe fails after a rollout
chunks.match: Readiness probe fails: pod is Running but never Ready

chunks.text:
Readiness probe fails after a rollout. Readiness probe fails: pod is Running but never Ready
## Verify
All pods are Ready and the Service lists endpoints again.
chunks.title: Readiness probe fails after a rollout
chunks.match: Readiness probe fails: pod is Running but never Ready

chunks.text:
Readiness probe fails after a rollout. Readiness probe fails: pod is Running but never Ready
## Escalate when
There is no previous revision, or pods of the previous revision are unready as well.
chunks.title: Readiness probe fails after a rollout
chunks.match: Readiness probe fails: pod is Running but never Ready

chunks.text:
Market data feed is stale while the pod looks healthy. Feed heartbeat gap or sequence gap warnings: market data is stale
## Recognise
Kubernetes shows the feed handler Running and Ready with no restarts. Its log has stopped printing ticks and repeats a warning about a heartbeat gap or a sequence gap, with the last sequence number frozen. Strategies downstream see prices that no longer move.
chunks.title: Market data feed is stale while the pod looks healthy
chunks.match: Feed heartbeat gap or sequence gap warnings: market data is stale

chunks.text:
Market data feed is stale while the pod looks healthy. Feed heartbeat gap or sequence gap warnings: market data is stale
## Why it happens
The session to the exchange gateway stalled without closing: a half-open TCP connection, a missed heartbeat during a network blip, or a multicast group that was dropped. The process is alive, so no probe fires.
chunks.title: Market data feed is stale while the pod looks healthy
chunks.match: Feed heartbeat gap or sequence gap warnings: market data is stale

chunks.text:
Market data feed is stale while the pod looks healthy. Feed heartbeat gap or sequence gap warnings: market data is stale
## Remediate
Restart the feed handler with rollout_restart. A new pod opens a new session and requests a snapshot, which is the same recovery a person would perform. The restart does not change the deployment's configuration.
chunks.title: Market data feed is stale while the pod looks healthy
chunks.match: Feed heartbeat gap or sequence gap warnings: market data is stale

chunks.text:
Market data feed is stale while the pod looks healthy. Feed heartbeat gap or sequence gap warnings: market data is stale
## Verify
New ticks appear in the log with increasing sequence numbers and the gap warning stops.
chunks.title: Market data feed is stale while the pod looks healthy
chunks.match: Feed heartbeat gap or sequence gap warnings: market data is stale

chunks.text:
Market data feed is stale while the pod looks healthy. Feed heartbeat gap or sequence gap warnings: market data is stale
## Escalate when
The gap warning returns after the restart. Then the fault is upstream, at the exchange or the network, and trading on stale prices must be stopped by a person.
chunks.title: Market data feed is stale while the pod looks healthy
chunks.match: Feed heartbeat gap or sequence gap warnings: market data is stale

chunks.text:
Pod cannot be scheduled. Pod cannot be scheduled: insufficient CPU or memory, taint or selector
## Recognise
The pod is Pending and the scheduler reports FailedScheduling with a count of nodes and a reason for each: Insufficient cpu, Insufficient memory, an untolerated taint or an unmatched node selector.
chunks.title: Pod cannot be scheduled
chunks.match: Pod cannot be scheduled: insufficient CPU or memory, taint or selector

chunks.text:
Pod cannot be scheduled. Pod cannot be scheduled: insufficient CPU or memory, taint or selector
## Why it happens
The pod asks for more than any node can offer, or the cluster lost capacity. Neither is a property of the pod that an agent may change safely.
chunks.title: Pod cannot be scheduled
chunks.match: Pod cannot be scheduled: insufficient CPU or memory, taint or selector

chunks.text:
Pod cannot be scheduled. Pod cannot be scheduled: insufficient CPU or memory, taint or selector
## Remediate
No automatic action. Lowering requests would let the pod start on a node that cannot carry it, and adding nodes is a spending decision.
chunks.title: Pod cannot be scheduled
chunks.match: Pod cannot be scheduled: insufficient CPU or memory, taint or selector

chunks.text:
Pod cannot be scheduled. Pod cannot be scheduled: insufficient CPU or memory, taint or selector
## Verify
Not applicable until a person has acted.
chunks.title: Pod cannot be scheduled
chunks.match: Pod cannot be scheduled: insufficient CPU or memory, taint or selector

chunks.text:
Pod cannot be scheduled. Pod cannot be scheduled: insufficient CPU or memory, taint or selector
## Escalate when
Always. Page the platform owner with the scheduler message and the pod's requests.
chunks.title: Pod cannot be scheduled
chunks.match: Pod cannot be scheduled: insufficient CPU or memory, taint or selector
